title: Token handoff for Ravel 2.0.0
intro: A confined harness receives a token that the owner minted, through an inherited socket. The owner agreed this route on 2026-11-03, and the implementation is ahead. Graph views start at the dark node labelled Start here, and numbered edge labels give the order of steps. The sequence starts at its first message. The specification docs/specs/token-handoff.md is the authority for every rule drawn here.

discussion.title: Hand a confined Claude Code an owner-minted token
discussion.status: Agreed by the owner on 2026-11-03. The specification is written and its review is integrated. The implementation is ahead
discussion.summary: The owner mints a token with claude setup-token and names its file in the settings. The configuration script names the handoff in a selection or a harness run. For a confined launch, Ravel checks the open file, reads it once and sends the token through a socket that the runner keeps open. Ravel never opens a sign-in store of a harness. No grant and no skill source may overlap the token file.

diagrams.title: From the owner's token to the confined Claude Code
diagrams.caption: The settings declare the file, the variable and the expiry date. The configuration script names the handoff. Ravel delivers it only under --confine. Every grant and every skill source that overlaps a protected path of the token file refuses, so no grant of a confined launch reaches the file. The handoff adds no Keychain or sign-in-store grant, and Ravel never opens the owner's own sign-in.

diagrams.title: Check, read and send in one confined launch
diagrams.caption: Ravel resolves the protected paths once, then checks the link count, the skill sources and the grants against them before the worker. After the selection, it resolves the declared path again, checks the open file and reads it, before it allocates the result channel. The runner grants each path in its checked form and keeps only the listed socket open across exec. A failed check or read launches nothing, and Ravel tries no other route. A harness run follows the same order for each run, and a failure there is the unavailable status that the script reads.

diagrams.title: Claude Code reads a socket directly and a pipe by its path
diagrams.caption: From the 2.1.317 executable. A probe under a copy of the profile used dummy text: the read of /dev/fd/3 failed with ENOENT for a pipe and for a socket, and the direct read passed for both. The branch inside Claude Code comes from minified code. A static reading in the review found that the direct reader closes the descriptor. The real-profile check of the implementation confirms the branch.

diagrams.title: Four rejected routes and the agreed route
diagrams.caption: The decision record a-confined-harness-receives-an-owner-minted-token gives each reason. The owner chose the first route before the conflict with Anthropic's terms and with Ravel's credential rule was found.
